rationale: Experience-store LLM routing; large cost cuts, but ablations on GAIA L1 only, no variance, and the test-stream update protocol is unclear.

paper.title: EvoRoute: Experience-Driven Self-Routing LLM Agent Systems
paper.central_claim: EvoRoute: a self-evolving, step-level model-routing policy for agentic systems that retrieves analogous prior steps from an ever-growing experience base, filters a Pareto-optimal set of LLMs over performance/cost/latency, and selects by Thompson sampling, sustaining or improving accuracy while cutting cost by up to 80% and latency by over 70%.

gap.author_gap: Agentic systems statically pre-assign LLMs to roles; existing routers target single-turn tasks or multi-agent roles on simple benchmarks, so deep-research agents face a performance/cost/latency 'trilemma'.
gap.checked_gap: The static, human-predefined role->model map is a real, checkable limitation with cited cost examples; the 'trilemma' is a framing rather than a measured law, and the paper offers no analysis of why prior routers fail at fine granularity beyond its own baseline numbers.
lineage: single-model routers (RouterBench-style, LLM-Blender, ZOOTER, cluster routers UniRoute/BEST-Route/Avengers) -> multi-agent routers (MasRouter, LLMSelector) -> step-level experience-driven routing (this work)
closest_adjacent: DSPy/TextGrad/ADAS-style automatic agent design (cited as 'fully automated')
gap.residue: Fine-grained, multi-turn, experience-conditioned routing for deep-research agents; baselines' use of equal experience data is unspecified.
gap.stakes: Per-task dollar cost up to ~$3 and ~40 minutes cited from prior systems; Table 1 shows >$350 per benchmark pass for Claude-4+CK-Pro.
gap.method_response: Per-step retrieval + Pareto + Thompson with an appended experience base.
gap.remaining_gap: Experience staleness/drift, store growth, benefit of continued evolution after cold start, more frameworks (authors' limitation).
unresolved: Whether experience-based routing beats a static role->model mapping tuned on the same 50 tasks.
Closest memory/routing neighbours not fixed locally.

matches.success_checks: No correspondence theorem (unmet); object formally defined in Eq.4 (met); no component deleted, retrieval pipeline added (unmet); faithfulness checked only by end metrics (partial).

matches.failure_checks: Cheaper alternative (static tuned role->model map, random routing) not tested (present).

G.reason: Concrete changed object (static role->LLM map) with cited cost examples and run baselines from three router families; nearest memory/auto-design neighbours and the boundary of the remaining gap are only partly drawn ('trilemma' is a framing).

M.reason: Pipeline from logged feedback to retrieval, Pareto filter and Thompson selection is explicit and fits the cost/latency problem; credit assignment copies task-level success to every step, Normal/NIG on bounded outcomes and hand-set weights are weakly justified.

X.reason: Core write/retrieve/select chain is specified, but there is no admission, deduplication, expiry or drift handling, the tree-based optimisation phase is not specified, and protocol for K updates during evaluation is unclear.

E.measurement.reason: Standard benchmark scorers; cost from token prices (Table 4); wall-clock delay is environment-dependent but reported consistently across methods.

E.causality.reason: Informative component ablations and router/single-model baselines exist, but ablations are L1-only single runs, no static-tuned-mapping or random-routing control, no frozen-vs-evolving K control, and baseline data parity is unspecified.

E.holdout.reason: Experience seeded from TaskCraft rather than the benchmarks (good), but whether K keeps updating on reported streams, hyper-parameter selection data, and contamination of K by benchmark-like items are unreported.

E.statistics.reason: Single run; no intervals; ablation conclusions rest on 53 tasks; some table percentages are not attainable as k/n for 53/26-task levels, indicating unreported averaging; task counts are given.

E.cost.reason: Cost and delay are primary reported metrics for all methods; cold-start cost ($28.8, 3.6 h) disclosed; routing overhead and baseline-router training costs not shown.
